correctness.rationale: The exact-block query definition and all boundary cases n=1 and singleton/full-support are explicit. All-positive labels enforce disjointness; a full cover with a singleton fails a designated negative labeling. The constructive partition realizes every remaining pattern with one unused buffer vertex or no singleton queries. Facets and coefficients follow from disjointness and labeled-block decompositions. Positive branches of any mistake tree reduce to n−|B| free elements, giving the induction Ldim≤n−1; n−1 singleton queries force the matching lower bound. Exhaustive independent trace tests checked 69,363 finite supports and the 1≤n≤4 online recurrences.

value.rationale: Exact-block cluster confirmation is a natural alternative query primitive in partition learning; the result classifies the entire nonpure shattering complex and its maximal faces, with explicit Stirling coefficients and exponential generating functions. The tight online dimension n−1 contrasts with Bell(n) candidate partitions. This resolves full combinatorial capacity, rather than a routine scalar special case. It does not imply optimal identification query counts or error robustness.
